headline: Picnic Grove and Planetarium Reservations
reservation: General park entry and hiking trails do not require reservations; picnic groves 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, and 24 require reservations for events from April 1 through November 30. Planetarium shows and indoor ranger programs at the Nature Center have limited seating and require checking the daily schedule upon arrival. The National Zoo, while adjacent, operates under a separate timed-entry system which must be checked independently.

days.title: Forest and Stars

stops.name: Rock Creek Nature Center
stops.detail: Explore the discovery room and check for planetarium showtimes to understand the park's wildlife.

stops.name: Western Ridge Trail
stops.detail: Hike the wooded elevations that run parallel to the city, offering a dense canopy and moderate terrain.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from the city center; rush hour traffic significantly impacts Beach Drive.
days.note: Trail surfaces can be muddy; sturdy closed-toe shoes are recommended even in an urban setting.

days.title: Historic Mills and Waterways

stops.name: Pierce Mill
stops.detail: Visit the last remaining 19th-century gristmill in the district to see the historic masonry and creek flow.

stops.name: Boulder Bridge
stops.detail: Photograph this iconic 1902 stone arch bridge, a landmark of the park's early design.

days.driving: Walking or cycling recommended on Beach Drive; allow 30 minutes for transit.
days.note: Upper Beach Drive is closed to motorized vehicles year-round; use open approach roads and explore the closed section on foot or by bicycle.

days.title: Equine Trails and Defenses

stops.name: Rock Creek Park Horse Center
stops.detail: Observe the stables and bridle paths that weave through the northern sections of the park.

stops.name: Fort DeRussy
stops.detail: Explore the earthwork remains of a Civil War fort nestled within the park's forest.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes for northern park access; parking varies by trailhead.
days.note: Northern trails offer more solitude compared to the high-traffic zoo-adjacent areas.

intel.title: Weekend Trailhead Limits
intel.text: Lots at the Nature Center and Pierce Mill often fill by 10 AM on sunny Saturdays. Consider using public transit to nearby Chevy Chase or Adams Morgan and walking in.

intel.title: Valley Bottom Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service frequently drops in the lower elevations near the creek bed. Carry a paper map or download digital versions before entering the Valley Trail.

intel.title: Urban Supply Access
intel.text: There are no fuel or food services within the park boundaries. Secure all supplies in the gateway neighborhoods of Silver Spring or D.C. before arrival.

intel.title: Beach Drive Recreation
intel.text: Portions of Beach Drive are closed to cars for weekend and holiday recreation. Check the NPS 'Operating Hours and Seasons' page for the specific street closure times.

intel.title: Accessibility and Paving
intel.text: The creek-side paths are largely paved and accessible, while the ridge trails feature natural, uneven terrain. Footbridges may become slippery during spring rains.

plan.arrival: Land at DCA and drive north for approximately 23 minutes. Check-in at D.C. or Bethesda hotels before heading to the Nature Center to orient yourself.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for all open park roads; no special equipment needed for this urban park.
plan.goldenHour: Photograph Boulder Bridge in late-afternoon light and finish your park walk before sunset; most park areas are open only from sunrise to sunset.
